name: John Heysham Gibbon Jr.
summary: American surgeon and medical researcher who invented the heart-lung machine.

name: Maly Gibbon
summary: Wife and research collaborator of John Heysham Gibbon Jr.

name: Princeton University
summary: University where Gibbon completed his undergraduate education.

name: Jefferson Medical College
summary: Medical school and hospital where Gibbon served as professor and performed the first successful open-heart surgery.

name: University of Pennsylvania
summary: University where Gibbon worked as Assistant Professor and conducted research.

name: Pennsylvania Hospital
summary: Hospital where Gibbon took up clinical work and served during the war.

name: Mayo General Hospital
summary: Hospital in Galesburg, Illinois where Gibbon served as Chief of Surgical Service during the war.

name: Heart-lung machine
summary: Apparatus developed by Gibbon to carry on circulation outside the body during surgery.

name: College of Physicians of Philadelphia
summary: Professional organization where Gibbon served as president.

name: Cecelia Bavolek
summary: Patient who underwent the first successful open-heart operation using the heart-lung machine.

name: I. S. Ravdin
summary: Director of the Harrison Department who funded Gibbon's improved machine model.

name: Jonathan Rhoads
summary: Surgical colleague and friend of Gibbon at the University of Pennsylvania.

name: Philadelphia
summary: City where Gibbon worked and lived.

name: Galesburg
summary: Location of Mayo General Hospital where Gibbon served during the war.

name: South Pacific
summary: Region where Gibbon served with the Pennsylvania Hospital Unit during the war.
